decisions.title: OpenAPI 3.2 default Schema Object dialect
decisions.issue: The released prose and published schema select different default OpenAPI 3.2 dialect URIs.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers disagree when a 3.2 Schema Object omits an explicit dialect.
decisions.selected_behavior: Apply the accepted correction and default to the dated OpenAPI 3.2 dialect.
decisions.rationale: The accepted correction resolves the contradiction without rewriting the pinned release.
decisions.security_consequences: Only checksum-pinned dialect resources are registered and no network access occurs.
decisions.resource_consequences: Dialect compilation remains bounded by compiler depth, node, operation, and cancellation limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Omitted 3.2 dialect declarations use corrected 3.2 vocabulary semantics.
decisions.wire_consequences: Explicit dialect declarations and source bytes remain unchanged.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenAPI correction #4994 was merged for the 3.2.1 patch line.
decisions.reconsider_when: A released OpenAPI patch changes the 3.2 dialect URI or precedence rules.

decisions.title: Paths, callbacks, webhooks, and extensions
decisions.issue: Path equivalence, callback and webhook traversal, custom operations, and extension interpretation have version-specific boundaries.
interpretations: Apply exact operation surfaces and preserve extensions as data
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers differ on ambiguous templates, callback and webhook traversal, custom methods, and extension recursion.
decisions.selected_behavior: Validate exact version operation surfaces, diagnose equivalent templates, traverse callbacks and webhooks, and keep extensions opaque unless explicitly handled.
decisions.rationale: Version-owned operation surfaces preserve normative behavior without granting extension data hidden semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Opaque extensions cannot trigger reference loading or hidden validation work.
decisions.resource_consequences: Nested operation traversal shares reference, node, depth, operation, diagnostic, and cancellation budgets.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Earlier documents do not inherit OpenAPI 3.2 custom-operation and repeated-template rules.
decisions.wire_consequences: Callbacks, webhooks, custom operations, and extension values round-trip in source order.
decisions.upstream_status: Version requirements and registered extension artifacts are separately pinned.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI changes path equivalence, operation surfaces, runtime expressions, or extension semantics.

decisions.title: Parameter serialization and ambiguous values
decisions.issue: Serialization defaults differ by version while nested deepObject, empty values, quoting, and delimiter collisions are undefined or implementation-defined.
interpretations: Support normative combinations and require explicit policy for ambiguous values
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers differ on form decoding order, repeated keys, empty values, and delimiter collisions.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use exact version defaults, reject undefined combinations, require an explicit empty-value policy, and use an explicit reversible percent-escape convention.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic failure is safer than guessing among multiple wire shapes.
decisions.security_consequences: Strict shape and delimiter handling prevents parameter smuggling through parser differentials.
decisions.resource_consequences: Byte and item limits apply before splitting, allocating, or decoding.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Normative examples and supported Swagger collection formats round-trip deterministically.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ambiguous delimiter values require the documented producer-consumer escape convention.
decisions.upstream_status: The conformance ledger maps each supported version's defaults and restrictions.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI defines nested, empty, cookie, header, or delimiter behavior now left undefined.

decisions.title: Security Requirement composition
decisions.issue: Security Requirement arrays, object members, anonymous alternatives, overrides, scopes, roles, and URI names are often flattened incorrectly.
interpretations: Treat every name as an alternative
Preserve OR across objects and AND within each object
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained middleware often models only one scheme and peers differ on role labels and URI-named schemes.
decisions.selected_behavior: Evaluate OR across requirement objects, AND within each object, preserve anonymous alternatives and explicit disablement, and apply exact version naming rules.
decisions.rationale: Preserving the normative composition boundary avoids authorization weakening.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed requirements fail closed and credential material is never logged or retained.
decisions.resource_consequences: Alternative, scheme, and scope counts are bounded before evaluation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: OpenAPI 3.1 role labels and 3.2 URI scheme names are accepted only in their versions.
decisions.wire_consequences: Compound, alternative, anonymous, and disabled requirements produce deterministic results.
decisions.upstream_status: Each version's composition and scheme-value requirements are recorded in conformance evidence.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI changes overrides, anonymous access, roles, URI names, or compound-scheme semantics.

decisions.title: Server URL template expansion
decisions.issue: OpenAPI requires substitution but does not define general component-aware escaping for server variable values.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained URI-template and OpenAPI tools differ on escaping, enum enforcement, undeclared variables, and unused overrides.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require valid declarations and defaults, apply literal substitution, make escaping caller-owned, and resolve references explicitly under RFC 3986.
decisions.rationale: Caller-owned escaping avoids hidden double encoding and delimiter transformations.
decisions.security_consequences: Expansion grants no network authority and invalid templates fail before destination use.
decisions.resource_consequences: Output bytes, declarations, overrides, and occurrences are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Defaults and overrides produce stable literal substitutions including repeated variables.
decisions.wire_consequences: Applications that require encoded values supply encoded bytes deliberately.
decisions.upstream_status: Literal replacement and caller-owned escaping are explicit package policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI defines component-aware encoding or adopts RFC 6570 expansion semantics.

decisions.title: JSON-equivalent YAML input
decisions.issue: General YAML features can represent values without one portable JSON meaning even though OpenAPI defines a JSON data model.
interpretations: Restrict YAML to one JSON-equivalent document
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers differ on aliases, merge keys, scalar inference, duplicate keys, and multi-document input.
decisions.selected_behavior: Accept one JSON-equivalent YAML document and reject aliases, merges, tags, non-string keys, duplicate keys, non-JSON scalars, and multiple documents.
decisions.rationale: One semantic model makes supported JSON and YAML representations equivalent.
decisions.security_consequences: Alias amplification and duplicate-key smuggling are rejected.
decisions.resource_consequences: Both parsers enforce byte, token, scalar, width, depth, cancellation, and diagnostic limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Inputs relying on general YAML features must be normalized by their producer.
decisions.wire_consequences: Supported YAML retains JSON member identity, ordering, scalar kinds, and exact number spellings.
decisions.upstream_status: The strict subset is package policy layered on OpenAPI's JSON data-model requirement.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI standardizes portable semantics for a currently rejected YAML feature.

decisions.title: HTTP reference representation selection
decisions.issue: OpenAPI does not define how remote reference media metadata and path extensions are reconciled.
interpretations: Treat explicit supported media types as authoritative
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers commonly infer JSON or YAML from filenames or content.
decisions.selected_behavior: Treat an explicit supported Content-Type as authoritative and use a recognized extension only when metadata is absent.
decisions.rationale: RFC 9110 warns against overriding received representation metadata.
decisions.security_consequences: A misleading path cannot downgrade explicit media metadata.
decisions.resource_consequences: Header and body handling remains under response, decompression, redirect, concurrency, timeout, and cancellation limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Servers with conflicting explicit media types are rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Responses without Content-Type retain deterministic extension-based selection.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenAPI defines no separate remote-reference representation selection algorithm.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI publishes remote-reference media selection rules.

decisions.title: Unpaired JSON surrogate escapes
decisions.issue: RFC 8259 permits parser limits but notes unpredictable behavior for unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained JSON implementations vary between rejection, replacement, and preservation.
decisions.selected_behavior: Reject unpaired high or low surrogate escapes while accepting valid escaped pairs.
decisions.rationale: Rejection preserves member and value identity instead of normalizing distinct bytes to U+FFFD.
decisions.security_consequences: Ambiguous identifiers and replacement-character collisions are rejected.
decisions.resource_consequences: The pre-scan is linear, allocation-free, and bounded by parser limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Inputs containing unpaired surrogate escapes are intentionally rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Valid Unicode and paired escaped scalar values remain unchanged.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 8259 explicitly allows implementations to set limits on accepted character contents.
decisions.reconsider_when: Go exposes a lossless standard representation and the package defines a compatible identity model.

decisions.title: Version-specific dialects and prose authority
decisions.issue: Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.x use incompatible Schema Object dialects and published schemas do not encode every prose rule.
interpretations: Validate every version with the newest schema
Use published schemas as sole authority
Dispatch exact versions and layer prose rules over pinned artifacts
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers differ on boolean schemas, OpenAPI 3.2 fields, validation depth, and prose-versus-schema authority.
decisions.selected_behavior: Dispatch exact supported versions and treat normative prose plus accepted errata as authoritative over published schemas.
decisions.rationale: Exact dispatch preserves each declared version instead of merging incompatible dialects.
decisions.security_consequences: Newer permissive vocabularies cannot bypass older constraints.
decisions.resource_consequences: Pinned artifact compilation and conversion remain depth, node, operation, and cancellation bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Documents retain the semantics of their declared exact version.
decisions.wire_consequences: Cross-version conversion reports semantic loss instead of inventing equivalence.
decisions.upstream_status: Pinned prose, accepted errata, schemas, dialects, and registries are tracked separately.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported patch changes dialect selection, prose authority, or conversion semantics.

decisions.title: Reference siblings, external resources, and cycles
decisions.issue: Reference sibling meaning, base URI selection, external loading, and legal versus destructive cycles differ across OpenAPI lines.
interpretations: Apply exact version rules and preserve cycles unless dereferencing would recurse
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained peers vary on reference siblings, cycle diagnostics, and implicit external loading.
decisions.selected_behavior: Apply exact version-specific siblings, explicit RFC 3986 bases, caller-authorized external loading, canonical cycle detection, and bounded graph traversal.
decisions.rationale: Reference semantics belong to the declared version and network authority belongs to the caller.
decisions.security_consequences: Resolution never grants ambient filesystem or network access and diagnostics redact resource identifiers.
decisions.resource_consequences: Depth, nodes, references, bytes, concurrency, redirects, decompression, and cancellation are bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: 3.0 ignores non-extension siblings while 3.1 and 3.2 apply only permitted overlays.
decisions.wire_consequences: Bundling and dereferencing preserve legal cycles or return classified errors without mutating source values.
decisions.upstream_status: The conformance ledger records each supported version's Reference Object rules.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenAPI changes Reference Object siblings, base resolution, or legal-cycle requirements.
